doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Why some musicians click right away
summary: Tanaka calls musical compatibility a kind of karma or mystery, with ego and style getting in the way.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Nice. Well someone asked last night, a student sort of asked a question about why are some musicians really compatible from the start almost. Can you answer that? Why a bass player and a piano player can really work together right from the beginning.

After eight years, I use like a karma. I don’t know why. Sometimes two musicians love the same kind of music and when they started they are both great musicians. But those two people never happen. Sometimes those things happen. But sometimes really great musicians, even if they play different kinds of music normally, but sometimes two musicians start to play, sometimes great things will happen. It’s kind of a mystery. It’s the same like general relationships too. Sports sometimes too. Those who start to play altogether not necessarily become a good team. Big ego. Too much big ego. And their own style.

That is a great analogy. When you think about the great people, Cannonball Adderley and Miles Davis, and those fellas didn’t play together that long because they were destined to be their own leaders.
